verdicts.reason: A demotes the CTA to a pill-sized chip and scatters it with the botanical pills in a ragged 2x3 grid inside the decorative circle. The pills have uneven heights and font sizes and butt against each other. The headline breaks to an orphan 'glow.', and the bottom third is dead space. B crams the CTA and all five pills into a tiny cluster jammed in the top-left corner, so the CTA is buried, and it also orphans 'glow.' and leaves the bottom empty. B is slightly less bad because the product and headline stay centred and read in order.

A is the same layout as pair 1's B: a buried CTA and pills cramped into the top-left corner, an orphaned 'glow.' and a large empty bottom. B keeps the headline on one line and puts the CTA and pills in a bottom block that reads in order. But the 'Build Your Mix' label is smaller than the pill labels, the pills touch or collide with uneven sizes, the logo has shrunk to a speck, and the legal line sits just under the headline where it is too prominent. B is still clearly the better structure.
